acs_race.note: ACS 5-year B03002 (Hispanic or Latino origin by race) per ZCTA, total population. The per-ZIP distribution the cohort draws `race` and `ethnicity` from, because CDC SVI's EP_MINRTY is one composite number and cannot say Black from Asian from Hispanic. Same keyless Summary File path as acs_veterans.

acs_veterans.note: ACS 5-year B21001 (sex by age by veteran status) per ZCTA, used to weight where the synthetic cohort is re-homed. NOTE: api.census.gov now 302s to missing_key.html for every request, so the keyed API is NOT a demo-day dependency; this Summary File path is keyless.

airnow_smoke.note: EPA AirNow daily files for the June 2023 Canadian-wildfire smoke episode plus a recent baseline week. NOTE: airnowapi.org needs a free key, but files.airnowtech.org is keyless and carries the same monitor data.

cooling_sites.note: NYC Parks Cool It! cooling sites (misting stations, spray showers, cool spots). Destination set for the cooling-center-ride action.

ehdp_geo_modzcta.note: MODZCTA -> UHF42 (the UHF most member ZCTAs sit in, from EHDP's zcta_to_uhf.csv) and community district (largest area overlap with EHDP's CD.geojson). Brings EHDP's neighbourhood rates onto the modzcta key. Needs the geo extra.

ehdp_heat.note: NYC EHDP heat ED visits and hospitalizations: indicators 2443 (5-year ED, 2018-22) and 2410 (10-year hospitalizations, 2013-22) by community district and borough, plus yearly 2075/2076 (UHF42 to 2014/2016). Number, annual rate and age-adjusted rate per 100,000. SPARCS counts < 11 are null with suppressed=True. Apache-2.0.

empower.note: HHS emPOWER: electricity-dependent Medicare beneficiaries per ZIP. Layer 1 = all DME, and it carries the O2 and ESRD-dialysis columns too.

evac.note: NYC Hurricane Evacuation Zones 1-6, area-weighted onto MODZCTA. This is the surge-exposure term and the join that would otherwise eat an hour of hackathon time.

floodnet_events.note: FloodNet street-flooding events with max depth and duration. Real observed pluvial floods, usable as a replay scenario instead of a scripted one.

floodnet_sensors.note: FloodNet sensor deployments with ZIP, borough and lat/lon. NOTE: floodnet.nyc gates its own API behind a request form, but the same data is open on NYC Open Data. No form needed.

heat_syndrome.note: NYC Health daily heat-syndrome ED visits, citywide, May-Sep 2017-2021, with the LaGuardia max of heat index and temperature. Apache-2.0. Syndromic: suspected, not confirmed, heat illness. 2021 is the publisher's 'live' file and may be revised.

hvi.note: NYC Heat Vulnerability Index 1-5, published per ZCTA20. The ZIP heat prior.

modzcta.note: NYC Modified ZIP Code Tabulation Areas: the map base and the spatial-join unit.

nri.note: FEMA National Risk Index, census tracts. Long-run heat-wave, hurricane, coastal-flood and riverine-flood hazard priors. NOTE: the old hazards.fema.gov static zip now 301s to a landing page; this FeatureServer is the live path.

nws_snapshot.note: A live snapshot of NWS active alerts and the 7-day gridpoint forecast for the five borough points. Keyless. Re-run on demo morning; the snapshot is the offline fallback.

places.note: CDC PLACES 2025, ZCTA level. Supplies the augment priors that were previously invented: mobility, self-care, independent living, loneliness, emotional support, utility shutoff, transport barrier, plus COPD/asthma/cancer/depression prevalence.

stormwater.note: NYC Stormwater Flood Maps (moderate 2.13 in/hr, current sea level), summarised to MODZCTA as flooded-area fraction. The Ida / pluvial term.

svi.note: CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index 2022, NY census tracts. Feeds the ZIP random-effect prior and the fairness strata.

synthea_med_profiles.note: One row per Synthea bundle: that patient's active RxNorm codes, sex, and age at their last recorded event. Distilled from the 30 MB FHIR sample so the cohort can give every synthetic veteran a real medication list -- co-prescribing intact -- without committing the bundles or reading data/raw/ at demo time.

synthea_sample.note: Synthea FHIR R4 sample bundles (~30 MB). The fixture the FHIR reader and its tests run against, so Track A is never blocked on the 4 GB VA release.

synthea_veteran_profiles.note: One row per living adult in the Synthea veteran run: sex, age, the Track A flags (ptsd, depression, diabetes, active_cancer_tx, suicide_risk, substance_use_disorder, homeless) and active RxNorm codes. The cohort draws whole profiles from it, so a veteran's diagnoses and prescriptions belong to one patient.

synthea_veterans.note: 15153 patients (living and dead) from Synthea v4.0.0; sha256 is the jar's, in full

va_drug_classes.note: RxNav exposes the VA's own 576-class drug taxonomy, keyless. This resolves every RxNorm code in the climate-risk crosswalk to its VA drug class offline, so the cohort can map Synthea prescriptions without calling RxNav at demo time.

va_facilities.note: VHA medical facilities with station number, address and lat/lon. NOTE: api.va.gov/services/va_facilities needs an approved developer.va.gov key; this mirror is keyless, which is why the build uses it.
